subject: Global compensation lattice: anchor refresh & benchmark artifacts
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Sun, 28 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Global compensation lattice: anchor refresh & benchmark artifacts

Team — attaching the first-pass deck and Mercer benchmarking CSV we received last week. High level asks below: 

1) Approve revised anchor points for L3-L7 for US / EU / APAC set; proposed deltas are +3% US anchor, -2% EU anchor, +6% APAC anchor (anchoring to local market medians).
2) Confirm acceptance of the proposed "lattice" model (flattened slope for L3-L5, steeper between L5-L7) so we can finalize leveling guidance.
3) Headcount impact: approximate FY27 incremental comp run-rate if we apply anchors across open hires and FY27 offers is ~$1.9M; see model tab in attached sheet. Need finance sign-off before we publish offers changes.

Open questions for the group: 
- Do we want to apply APAC uplift uniformly or allow country-level overrides for high-cost cities?
- How should promotion ladders interact with the new lattice (especially between L4->L5 where slope changes)?

Please review slide 6 (benchmarks) and the model tab in the workbook. Looking for a decision by EOD next Thursday (2027-04-01) so HR can bake new bands into the offer generator.

Attachments: comp_lattice_proposal_v1.pptx, mercer_geobenchmarks_2027.csv, headcount_impact_model_2027.xlsx

Thanks —
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Director, Rewards & Talent Strategy
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Global compensation lattice: anchor refresh & benchmark artifacts

Thanks, Soojin — reviewed slides and the Mercer CSV. A few notes: 

- I agree with flattening the slope L3-L5; that should help closing offers faster in competitive markets.
- For APAC uplift, recommend we keep a country-level override for Singapore and Sydney given cost differentials.
- Finance will want a clearer phasing plan (Q2 vs Q3 apply to open offers vs full-band reset). Can Marissa provide a 2-scenario projection (immediate vs phased) in the model?

Also tagging hiring managers: we'll need a short comms template for managers to explain band changes to candidates.

Laura
Laura Bennett
VP, People Operations

Attached: headcount_impact_model_2027.xlsx (updated). I built two scenarios in separate tabs: 1) Immediate apply across all open offers and re-pricing existing offers in pipeline; 2) Phased: only new offer generator uses new bands starting 2027-07-01, existing accepted offers/hire commitments grandfathered. Highlights: immediate = +$1.9M run-rate; phased = +$0.95M first year.

I also added a comms draft for managers on tab 'comms_draft'. Quick ask: can Karthik sign off on promotion ladder interaction? If we make L4->L5 midpoint expansion optional, managers may use discretion and that complicates calibration. Suggest we create a small exception workflow instead of broad optionality.

Attachments: headcount_impact_model_2027.xlsx

—Marissa
Marissa Cole

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 17:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Global compensation lattice: anchor refresh & benchmark artifacts

Thanks for the thoughtful package. A few quick decisions from my side so we can close: 

- Approve the lattice orientation (flatten L3-L5, steeper above L5).
- Approve country-level overrides for APAC with explicit callouts for Singapore and Sydney.
- Promotion ladder: do NOT make L4->L5 midpoint expansion optional at large; instead we will use an exception approval flow (HR + Manager + People Ops) for individual promotions that exceed the new midpoint range. Karthik will own a short SOP for this.
- Phasing: finance prefers the phased approach (apply to new offers starting 2027-07-01, reprice only on manager-requested retables), so we go with Marissa's Scenario 2.

Action items: 
- Marissa: finalize the model and lock the phased scenario; add a brief sensitivity tab for 5%/10% market swings.
- Soojin: draft manager comms and the exception approval flow doc; route for Legal/Finance review by 2027-04-08.
- Laura/Tessa: once docs are ready, coordinate a short sync with Hiring Managers (30 min) the week of 2027-04-12.

I'll publish a one-page decision memo after Soojin's doc is ready.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
VP, Talent & Org Design
